classification.difficultyReason: Identify congruent right-angled triangles within a practical diagram, justify corresponding lengths and convert paces to metres.

content.prompt: A scout wants to estimate the width of a river. On the opposite river bank there is a tree $T$. The scout marks a point $A$ on his side of the river directly opposite $T$. He then goes 6 paces along the river bank perpendicular to $AT$ and marks a point $B$, then continues a further 6 paces to mark a point $C$. The scout then walks away from the river, at a right angle to $BC$, to a point $D$ where $B$ and $T$ are in a line. From $C$ to $D$ is 7 paces.

spec.description: A vertical river strip is identified by diagonal hatching. A, B and C occur in that order on the left bank; T is opposite A, and D is left of C. D, B and T are collinear. Right-angle marks are at A and C. Distances remain in the stem only.
spec.mathematics: AB = BC; AT is perpendicular to AC; CD is perpendicular to AC; D, B and T are collinear.
spec.answerVisibility: No calculated lengths or congruence conclusions appear in the question diagram.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Approximately how many paces wide is the river?

answer.short:
Approximately 7 paces.

The two triangles are congruent by AAS, so $AT=CD$.
answer.worked:
In triangles $ABT$ and $CBD$:

$\angle BAT=\angle BCD=90^\circ$ (given right angles).

$\angle ABT=\angle CBD$ (vertically opposite angles).

$AB=CB=6$ paces (given).

Therefore $\triangle ABT\equiv\triangle CBD$ (AAS), so $AT=CD=7$ paces (matching sides of congruent triangles).

The river is approximately 7 paces wide.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the scout’s pace is 0.8 m long, approximately how wide is the river in metres?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{River width}&=7\times0.8\text{ m}\\\text{River width}&=5.6\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$
The river is approximately $5.6\text{ m}$ wide.
